task.description: WF-03 Step 4: write test spec and test code for ISS-0389's advance-timer endpoint (design doc AC1-AC10), un-skip the REQ-206 shipment-ops-timeout-escalation scenario's step 2 per AC5/AC10, and route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.

result.summary: Full test spec at test/specs/ISS-0389.md. (1) Letflow.Scheduler.resolve_advance_target/3 had ZERO tests referencing it by name before this run (confirmed by grep) -- added 9 tests across two new describe blocks in test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs covering all 7 of the design's own branch outcomes: 0/1/2+ pending timers with timer_id absent, and not-found/not-pending(fired)/wrong-instance/correct for an explicit timer_id (the 'same-404' fold). (2) test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs had NO advance-timer tests at all -- added a new 'advance-timer' describe block (8 tests) plus graph_timer_end/0, start_instance_with_timer!/1, pending_timer_ids/2 helpers, covering AC5 (200/fired/token-off-TIMER, proven end-to-end via instance_status becoming :completed on a TIMER->END graph), AC6 (404, zero pending), AC7 (400, 2+ pending, both remain pending), AC8 (404, cross-instance timer_id, neither timer fires), AC9 (422 x2, instance_id and timer_id), design's own 'body not a JSON object' 400 case, and a dedicated 403 authz-enforcement test for :InstancesAdvanceTimer (distinct from the generic route-walk AC4 already covers). (3) Un-skipped shipment-ops-timeout-escalation.yaml step 2 (via:skip -> via:api) per AC5/AC10, rewrote req206_swiftroute_test.exs's matching describe block to assert real outcomes (timer_status: fired, node_id: ops-escalation-timer, and current_nodes read directly off instance_projections since GET /instances/:id's own response shape carries no tokens field -- only POST /:id/reconstruct does). (4) Added a real ops-escalation-timer TIMER node to process_shipment_dispatch.yaml (fork branch parallel to ops-assessment/finance-estimate feeding parallel-join) since the pre-existing timeout-ops-assessment edge was a comment-only annotation, never a real REQ-187 timer mechanism -- HUMAN_TASK has no boundary-timer capability in this engine. (5) Fixed two pre-existing bugs surfaced only by actually dispatching this fixture for the first time (never previously exercised end-to-end): (a) req206_swiftroute_test.exs's own ops-timeout-escalation test destructured the WRONG definition (%{approval: ...} instead of %{dispatch: ...}), inert while step 2 was a no-op :skip; (b) process_shipment_dispatch.yaml's parallel-fork was a :combined_unsupported gateway (in_degree>1 AND out_degree>1) that Engine.create/2 correctly rejects -- fixed with a new pure-merge injury-check-merge EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY node. Both fixes documented in the fixture's own header comment and the test spec.
